title: Do not disturb, quiet-hours schedules and urgent break-through, visible to agents
summary: Add a per-user attention state {dnd_until, schedules [{days, start, end, tz}], vip subjects} to notification-core and gate the router on it: while in DND, non-critical signals from non-VIP actors are stored for the inbox only and do not go to push or the OS, then flush when DND ends. Agents classify approval requests by urgency in capability-core, with a per-agent daily cap and an owner-configurable limit on critical break-through. Expose a coarse 'can I interrupt now' answer to agents, not the schedule itself.
whyItMatters: Agents work around the clock. Without DND they will page humans at night, and push (F-t1-035 (R-t1-05-05)) should not ship before this gate. It also helps the agents: one that can check whether a human is interruptible can defer a non-urgent ask instead of blocking a run.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack (manual pause, schedule, admin default hours, VIP and urgent break-through); Teams for urgent messages and meeting auto-DND
others: Teams (priority contacts, urgent messages, auto-DND in meetings)
Buzz (explicitly has none; spec defers DND)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Slack combines a manual pause, a recurring schedule, admin default hours, a VIP override and a once-a-day 'notify anyway' urgent break-through (DOC). Teams adds urgent messages and priority contacts that pass DND and automatic DND in meetings (REA). Router rule: if the user is in DND, the signal is not critical and the actor is not VIP, store it in the inbox only and do not deliver to OS or push; queued items flush when DND ends; urgent break-through is rate-limited per sender.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: No DND, quiet hours or schedule exists in Spaces or notification-core (channels.go holds only org-level event-by-channel configuration). Quiet hours are named as part of S4.4, whose current source state is the delivery attempt state machine and a disabled-by-default worker.

approachOriginal: Application Plane (notification-core): attention-state table and a router gate placed after the F-t1-008 (R-t1-05-04) preference checks. Model Plane (capability-core): add an urgency class to approval and agent-awaiting signals, plus a per-agent daily critical cap. Frontend Plane: DND toggle, schedule editor and VIP list in Settings. Expose DND to agents only through a narrow 'interruptible now' read so the schedule itself is not disclosed to every room member's agents.
risks: Urgent-flag abuse by agents (cap per agent per day, owner-configurable); disclosing a user's schedule to agents or room members; queued items must flush once and in order.

alreadyPlanned.where: S4.4 quiet hours: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md (execution tracker, line 226) and the baseline note 'Quiet hours are planned in S4.4'

verevon.exactGap: Control user-core already stores a per-user NotificationSettings.QuietHours {enabled, start, end} (default off, 22:00-08:00) and a manual profile availability status (online/busy/away/offline, labelled as helpdesk behaviour), but nothing enforces or exposes them: the frontend has no quiet-hours UI and notification-core's only gate is a per-event opt-out (WithPreferenceGate, IsNotificationEnabled) with no time window, DND, VIP or urgency class. No Space event producers reach notification-core either (the sender allow-list is gateway 'notification.created' for the delegated user and capability-core run_completed/run_failed), and a gate-suppressed request is stored as suppressed and returns before dispatch, so it neither reaches push nor creates an inbox row.
reuse: user-core NotificationSettings and QuietHours (GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/notifications) as the source of truth to extend with timezone, days, dnd_until and VIP
notification-core WithPreferenceGate seam in Accept (service.go isNotificationEnabled) as the enforcement point, and the existing suppressed status
notification-core identity_sync NATS consumer as the pattern for projecting a user attention setting from Control into notification-core
AccountSettingsPage Availability section as the UI host and the existing profile status field
activity-grammar.ts salience classes (critical, attention, normal, muted) as the urgency vocabulary for approval and awaiting signals
verevon.constraints: DND is a person-level attribute that spans organisations, while notification-core rows and every Space or Model event are org-scoped, so keep the source of truth in Control user-core and project it into notification-core by event or API, never by cross-plane DB read. The existing gate is binary (suppressed or sent) and drops the inbox row too, so DND needs a tri-state (deliver, inbox-only, deferred) and a flush path; the delivery queue is off by default and rejects ZDR requests, so flush depends on finishing the S4.4 ledger (F-t1-060). Urgency must be set by the trusted producer (gateway or capability-core), not by the agent, with a per-agent cap; the 'interruptible now' answer to agents must be a narrow server-side read bound to the run's delegated subject that does not disclose the schedule or cross orgs. Quiet hours are already named in S4.4, and space-defenition.md lists 'notification polish' in its non-goals, so this is planned but only partly aligned with the stated non-goal.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Start from the existing user-core quiet-hours setting instead of a new attention-state table: add timezone (the profile already has one), days, dnd_until and VIP, project it into notification-core, and add the gate after the preference check with a deliver/inbox-only/defer decision. Sequence it after the Space notification producers (F-t1-008) exist, because there is nothing Space-specific to gate today, and fold the deferred flush into the single S4.4 ledger rather than a second queue.
verevon.effortNote: M holds for settings, gate and UI; the flush rides on the S4.4 ledger (F-t1-060) and the producers are separate items.
verevon.verdictReason: The item says no quiet hours exist, but a stored-and-unenforced per-user quiet-hours setting and a profile availability status already exist in Control; the build should extend them and respect the person-level versus org-scoped split.

title: Finish the S4.4 delivery ledger and add a content-free missed-activity digest
summary: Generalise notification-core's lease-based delivery-attempt ledger into the S4.4 Space delivery ledger: idempotency keys, max-age expiry, bounded retries, and delivery errors reported back to the agent run that produced the message. Then add an email channel and a per-user digest (hourly or daily) that auto-pauses after inactivity and, for ZDR orgs, carries counts and links only.
whyItMatters: The ledger is the foundation for push, email digests, scheduled agent output and the future Channel Plane without losing or duplicating messages. The digest pulls absent humans back when agents are blocked on them, cutting approval latency.

others: Buzz (content-free mention outbox bridged by an operator)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Outbox: 2 of 5 sources, differentiator; digest: 2 of 5, common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: QM's DeliveryStore does enqueue, claimPending and ack with idempotency keys, max-age expiry and 5 retries, and reports undeliverable errors back to the source session; its personal morning digest runs on a managed schedule that auto-pauses when the person is inactive. Teams-style missed-activity email summarises unread mentions and activity. Outbox row: id, idempotency_key, destination, source_ref, status, attempts, lease_until, with a reaper for stale leases.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: notification-core already has a leased delivery-attempt state machine (pending, claimed, sent_unconfirmed, acknowledged, failed, unknown) whose worker is disabled by default, but the Space delivery ledger is only a named gap (delivery_ledger_not_built) and the plan's tracker still lists durable feed reconciliation, provider and ZDR proof and HA as open. There is no email channel for Space events and no digest of any kind.

approachOriginal: Application Plane: extend notification-core's attempt ledger into the S4.4 Space ledger, keeping its semantics (provider acceptance is not confirmation; ambiguous outcomes stay 'unknown'; ZDR attempts content-free). Add idempotency keys and a reply-to-source error path for agent runs. Model Plane (capability-core schedule) composes the digest and notification-core delivers it, with counts and links only for ZDR orgs. Avoid a second parallel ledger for notifications versus Space delivery.
dependencies: Provider and ZDR proof for any third-party sender
risks: Two ledgers diverging if not unified; email is a content-persisting boundary outside Verevon, so a ZDR org's digest must carry no bodies; digest fatigue without inactivity auto-pause.

alreadyPlanned.where: S4.4 durable Space completion delivery: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md (execution tracker, line 226); named gap delivery_ledger_not_built in apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:1618-1622

verevon.exactGap: notification-core has a leased delivery-attempt state machine (pending, claimed, sent_unconfirmed, acknowledged, failed, unknown), a lease-fenced worker and request-level idempotency keys, but the worker is off by default, needs NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_MODE=novu plus a callback secret, has no bounded-retry or max-age policy, and rejects ZDR requests outright (service.go:296-301, delivery_worker.go:91-94). The Space delivery ledger is a named gap (delivery_ledger_not_built, spaces.rs:1618-1623) with no Space-event producers, and no per-user digest exists: insight-core's daily-brief scheduler (per-org/day idempotency key, email channel registered in migration 006) is deliberately disabled because an organisation is not a notification recipient.
reuse: notification-core delivery_attempts state machine, lease-fenced worker and callback verifier as the single ledger (do not build a parallel Space ledger)
notification-core request idempotency keys (FindByIdempotencyKey and resumeExisting) and insight-core BriefIdempotencyKey (daily_brief_<org>_<day>) as the digest dedupe pattern
insight-core briefs scheduler shape (round per tick, per-recipient key) and the channel-config registry rows for email (migrations 006 and 013)
Convex outbox lease pattern (spaceLifecycleEvents deliveryState, lease, nextAttemptAt) and ctx.scheduler.runAfter workers for a Space-side outbox or digest tick
notification-core identity_sync consumer pattern for event-fed user state
verevon.constraints: ZDR: notification-core refuses to enqueue ZDR requests today because the queue stores no payload and no transient-descriptor provider contract exists, so a ZDR org's counts-and-links digest cannot ride the existing queue; it needs an explicit content-free request class or retention mode ruled on by Control/ZDR policy, or the encrypted expiry-bound descriptor contract the code comment names. Email goes through Novu to an external provider, a content-persisting boundary whose provider and ZDR proof the S4.4 tracker still lists as open. Recipients must be real user subjects (the gateway may notify only the delegated user; an org id is not a recipient), and digest counts must come from Application-owned state (read markers, inbox feed) or owner-plane APIs and events, never DB reads, since pending approvals live in Model Plane. Digest links must resolve through normal Space membership checks (membership_changed revocations apply), so Space access never widens.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Treat finishing the S4.4 ledger (bounded retries, max-age, ZDR proof, durable feed reconciliation, HA) as the already-planned dependency rather than new work, and make the digest a separate Application Plane item: a per-user scheduler modelled on insight-core's briefs scheduler (using Convex scheduler or an outbox) that composes counts and links, instead of a capability-core Space schedule, because a digest is a projection and capability-core schedules fire Model runs needing Control fire decisions. Add the reply-to-source error path for agent runs as a Model-side change tracked separately. Gate any ZDR-org digest on the content-free request class decision.
verevon.effortNote: Kept at L, but note the split: the digest alone is M once the ledger and a content-free class exist; finishing the ledger is roadmapped S4.4 work and larger than the digest.
verevon.verdictReason: Status is partial and already planned (S4.4); the item understates what exists (idempotency keys, lease worker, email channel config, a disabled brief scheduler), overstates what ZDR allows (the queue rejects ZDR), and places digest composition in the wrong plane.

title: 'Catch me up' recap of what I missed, scoped to my own read access
summary: Add a 'Catch me up' entry point on the room header and the inbox. It runs a Model Plane recap turn over the unread messages and runs since the user's last read marker, prioritising items that mention the user or need action, with scopes unread, last 7 days or a custom range, and offers mark-as-read on completion. The scope is computed from the viewer's own access, ZDR is propagated, and the result is ephemeral for ZDR orgs.
whyItMatters: The highest-value AI feature for a returning user in an agent-heavy room: what did the agents do while I was away, and what needs me. Verevon owns its Model Plane and already puts agents in rooms, so this is an agent turn rather than a new subsystem, and it is the sort of attention feature Slack and Teams only bolt on.

others: Slack (unread-only, last 7 days or custom range, plus a recurring-summary workflow step)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Teams does a holistic, cross-thread recap prioritised by relevance, with read-aloud, and marks chats read when the recap is dismissed (REA). Slack offers unread-only, last-7-days and custom-range scopes and a workflow step for recurring summaries (DOC). Collect unread content since last_read for the requested scope (only content the viewer can access), summarise with a model, prioritise mentions and action items, offer mark-as-read.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Only a 'Meeting Scribe' agent template that summarises the text conversation when it is mentioned. There is no 'catch me up' entry point, no unread-scoped or cross-room recap and no link to read markers.

approachOriginal: Frontend Plane: 'Catch me up' action in the room header and the inbox, registered in the action registry. Model Plane: a recap run invoked with the viewer's own read scope (never a wider room scope), zdr=true propagated, token and cost limits through the existing cost plane. Use the unread map and read markers from F-t1-009 (R-t1-05-02) to pick the window; optionally mark-as-read on completion. Output is not persisted for ZDR orgs.
dependencies: F-t1-009 (R-t1-05-02) read markers and unread map
Model Plane run with viewer-scoped access
planeOwner: Model Plane (recap run); Frontend Plane (entry point)
risks: Summaries quoting content the viewer cannot see if the scope is computed from the room rather than the viewer; cost on large rooms; stale recap if new messages arrive mid-run.

verevon.exactGap: The 'Catch me up' feature itself is absent: no catch-up action, recap run or unread-scoped summary exists in features/spaces or the gateway, and the only related thing is the Meeting Scribe agent template, which summarises the thread when mentioned and posts into the room for everyone. The substrate the item lists as a dependency is already shipped: an Application read marker per member per room (spaceReadMarkers.ts, spaces.mark_read action), an arrival-time snapshot and unread set (space-unread.ts, SpacePage.tsx), unread dots in the sidebar, and viewer-scoped transcript and work reads under Control read decisions (space_thread_transcript, space_work). The marker is a room-level timestamp over threads, not per message.

reuse: Application read marker and the arrival-marker snapshot as the window start
space_thread_transcript and space_work reads (per-viewer Control decisions) as the content source
sidebar and room-header unread signals as entry points
spaces.mark_read action for the mark-as-read on completion step

model-gateway budget guard for cost limits
verevon.constraints: The recap must read only what the viewer may read: gather transcripts through the existing per-thread Control read decisions and the work projection, never a room-wide Model Plane scope, and bound the number of unread threads because decisions are per thread. The output is viewer-private, so it must not be posted into the room (a mention-driven Scribe reply is visible to every member); keep it ephemeral or store it in the viewer's personal Space. ZDR: a ZDR turn is a single stateless call, which fits an ephemeral recap; non-ZDR orgs need an explicit persistence choice. Application owns the read marker (timestamp only), Model Plane owns the recap call, Control owns the read decisions.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Put the entry points where the unread signal lives: the room header and the sidebar or Spaces list for cross-room recap, not the Inbox, which is the support ticket inbox with no Space unread state. Build it as a gateway-composed stateless summarize call (threads read under the viewer's Control decisions plus the run list since the arrival marker) instead of a new Model Plane run primitive with viewer-scoped multi-thread access, which does not exist, and avoid the room-agent persona path because it would post the answer to the room. Use the arrival snapshot, not the advancing durable marker, as the window start. The item's dependency on F-t1-009 read markers is already met at room level.
verevon.effortNote: M holds if the recap is stateless and gateway-composed; it becomes L if a persisted private result surface is added.
verevon.verdictReason: The feature is genuinely missing and cheap relative to its value, but the item misses that its read-marker dependency is shipped, points at the wrong inbox, and assumes a viewer-scoped Model Plane run primitive that does not exist; the stateless gateway-composed route is the buildable path.

title: Space UI quality baseline: locale-correct activity grammar and dates, server-held preferences, shared announcer, reduced motion, density and high contrast, failure screens
summary: Move the hard-coded Norwegian activity labels and forced nb-NO dates onto the i18n catalogue and the viewer locale (and pass the locale to the Model Plane); move locale and time zone into a layered, versioned user/org preference document next to the already server-side theme; promote the page-local live region into a shared, tick-keyed announcer with row narration and focus hand-off rules; audit Space animation for prefers-reduced-motion and add a density setting; add forced-colors/prefers-contrast rules for status marks and focus rings; and add a cannot-reach-Verevon page with start-up milestones.
whyItMatters: Verevon's Space accessibility and bilingual UI are already at or above buzz and QM; these small gaps (Norwegian-only activity grammar, no high-contrast rules, split preference storage) are where it would regress as the room grows.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (friendly activity vocabulary, announcer and pane focus rules); Teams (row narration, start-up milestones); Slack (cannot-connect page with log download); Buzz (reduced-motion gate, 3-level density); teams (63 locales with regional fallback map, app locale independent of the OS locale) for localization; slack (validated layered settings object with effective-value view) for preferences
others: grokbot (RTL, endonyms, zod-versioned settings that refuse bad files)
qm (palette import with contrast checks, density tiers)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-12-11] friendly copy 2 of 5 (Grok Bot, QM); accessibility 2 of 5 (Grok Bot, Teams); motion/density 2 of 5 (Buzz, Teams); shell failure UX 2 of 5 (Slack, Teams); differentiators [R-t1-11-06] Localization 3 of 5 (common); theming and high contrast 4 of 5 (table-stakes); preference store 3 of 5 (common).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-12-11] Catalog map from activity kind to localised friendly label. Announcer: two hidden regions (role=status, role=alert) each wrapping a span keyed by a counter so identical messages repeat, with announce(text, politeness). Pane navigation: outgoing pane inert and aria-hidden until animationend, then focus to the landing target once headings exist, skipped if focus is already elsewhere. Density: a data attribute scaling spacing variables; motion components check prefers-reduced-motion. Failure UX: milestone events (loaderStarted, firstPaint) to telemetry, critical load failure routes to an error page listing network checks and a "download logs" bundle. [R-t1-11-06] Message catalogs keyed by id with ICU plurals and a fallback chain; dir=rtl; Intl dates in the user locale. Preference schema with version and migrations; layers default < org policy < user < device; read API returns value plus source. Theme tokens as CSS variables with system, light, dark and contrast modes; org branding from config.

Create shared/lib/announcer and route Space completions and approvals through it, polite by default and assertive only for approvals addressed to the viewer. Add a root boundary and a static gateway-served fallback page; the diagnostic bundle must redact tokens and exclude ZDR content. Control Plane (user-core / org-core): a versioned preference document with layered resolution exposed through the navbar/bootstrap payload (migrating the localStorage locale on first load); org branding fields (accent, mark) with contrast enforced at save time. Model Plane reads time zone and language for scheduled agent work.

title: Agent identity in the room: surface the persisted avatar colour (then shape) and add a hover card that leads with blocking state
summary: Pass the avatarColor that the Application Plane already stores and projects through the gateway agent composition and the SpaceAgent type, then render a deterministic non-human shape-by-colour avatar on posts, agent cards, the roster and the sidebar. Add a hover/focus card for agents and members whose preview leads with what blocks a human (awaiting approval), then a draft, then the last entry.
whyItMatters: Agents must be instantly distinguishable from people in a mixed room and must never look like a human colleague. The colour is already collected and stored, so this is a bug-level fix with immediate visible effect; the hover card surfaces "waiting for your approval" wherever an agent name appears.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (14+ shapes by 11 colours, crop upload, describe-to-generate; hover card ordered by blocking state)

title: Room creation flows: templates with an agent roster and seed artifacts, clone, project and case Spaces bound to work objects, invite-on-mention
summary: Let a room be created from a declarative template (description, instructions, agent roster bound through the normal bind decision, seed canvas and list) or cloned from an existing room, in one transaction; enable project and case kinds with owner and roster, and have the Application Plane create a bound case or project Space when a ticket, customer case or project is created (membership from assignees, owner-plane ACLs stay authoritative, agent bindings still need human approval). When someone mentions a non-member or unbound agent, offer to add or bind them through the normal decisions.
whyItMatters: Buzz's templates with an agent roster are something neither Slack nor Teams has, and case Spaces are already planned in the Space authority ADR; together they turn recurring work into ready-made human-plus-agent rooms.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (templates, non-member mention dialog); Buzz (SRC): a resource event lists coordinates and binds a channel, and the project signer gets no authority over member resources
others: qm (project rooms with source-tracked channel members)

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-02-11] templates 2 of 5 (buzz, teams; differentiator); project rooms 1 of 5 (qm); mention-to-invite 1 of 5 (buzz); unique to differentiator [R-t1-08-09] resource-bound rooms: 1 of 5, unique; templates: 1 of 5, unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-02-11] room_template(id, name, visibility, description, canvas_ref, agents[{definition_id, role, policy}]); instantiate creates the room then binds each agent through the normal decision. On send the server returns non_member_mentions[]; the client shows a dialog (safe action focused, invite withheld and explained when the actor cannot administer the room, draft restored on cancel); invite goes through the normal add-member decision. QM project store keeps channel-derived members separate so unlinking removes only them. [R-t1-08-09] Binding record {resource_ref, space_ref} created with the resource; a project is a list of resource refs plus a home space and only aggregates, since each resource's authorization still comes from its owner. A template is a declarative bundle {room settings, artifacts[], agents[]} instantiated in one transaction.

summary: Give skills a Space scope and a review lifecycle (draft, reviewed, published, archived, with review invalidated by any edit and signed manifests), and let the org plugin registry accept Claude-style and Cursor-style marketplace manifests with git-sha pinning and a variables schema, fanning components out to the skill store, MCP registry and hook runner. A Space manager can then enable an org-activated plugin or publish a room skill, never beyond what the org allows.
whyItMatters: A team can curate room-specific know-how ('how we run incident review') safely, which is how agents get better in a shared room, and reading existing plugin ecosystems gives Verevon agents many capabilities for little effort. Grok Bot reads both .cursor-plugin and .claude-plugin marketplace.json, pins git sources to a 40-hex sha, declares a variables JSON-schema (writeOnly marks secrets) and registers each component (commands, agents, skills, rules, hooks, mcpServers) with its subsystem; buzz persona packs are a simpler variant.

title: Duplex voice for agents: a voice front that delegates to the Space agent, then agents as attributed participants in room calls
summary: Phase A (M, no SFU needed): inside a Space, a user holds a realtime voice conversation with an agent. A fast voice persona talks and its only tools delegate: send_task hands real work to the existing agent run in the Space (still behind approval gates) and a history search covers Space threads and past voice sessions; each agent gets voice, speed and language settings. Phase B (L, after F-t1-029 (R-t1-03-01)): a server-side participant per invited agent hears the call through STT, answers with an attributed audio track, and stops when a human starts talking.
whyItMatters: This is the defining hybrid moment of the Space vision: humans and agents in the same voice room, and a personal agent that can be tasked hands-free. The front and worker split avoids a second agent brain, and doing it server-side is better than Buzz, whose agent voice runs on the owner desktop.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (SRC) for the voice-front and worker split; Buzz (SRC) for agents as audio participants with floor control
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grok Bot: realtime session (session.update, input_audio_buffer.append, response.create/cancel) with voice tools send_task(constraints), recall_text_messages and search_conversations{query, scope this-chat|earlier|everything, from, to, if_missing}; worker results come back as async updates the persona announces; one active voice chat per user and ending needs confirmation; the refusal text for send_task tells the model not to drop prohibitions or approval requirements; per-agent voice_id, voice_speed, voice_language. Buzz: agent audio publisher authenticates as the agent and shows in the roster; VAD with about 300 ms silence flush; any human speech cancels agent TTS (barge-in); agent speaks only when addressed.

The baseline also records that personal agents are not possible today (a personal Space cannot hold an agent), which limits a personal-agent voice phase until that is changed.

approachOriginal: Model Plane: a realtime voice session type whose only tools are send_task (calls the existing agent run API in the Space so approval gates and Control decisions still apply) and search_conversations (Space threads read under the read decision); add voice_id, voice_speed and voice_language to the agent profile in the registry behind SpaceCreateAgentDialog. Enforce F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-03) before the agent hears the room.

Agents in personal Spaces (agents-in-the-room category) for personal-agent voice
risks: ZDR attestation for realtime providers (the route already fails closed). Cost per minute. Agents talking over humans; always label agent voices. Delegated actions must still hit in-room approval gates and must carry the constraints of the spoken request.

verevon.constraints: A realtime session hands the browser a client secret and a direct provider socket, so the Model Plane cannot meter cost, enforce tools server-side or see the audio; tool calls must be executed by the browser through the normal BFF Space send and approval path, and the Space context has to be pinned in the session instructions at mint time. ZDR voice is refused today, so ZDR Spaces get no duplex voice. History search needs a Space read decision. Agents speak only when invited (invocation rule), which matches the item. title: Make zero-data-retention binding in every plane, with typed refusals and content-free telemetry
summary: Session Core must act on the zero_data_retention flag in the signed Control decision (today it decodes the flag and discards it): refuse durable thread, message and memory writes under ZDR with a typed code. Prove the same for the other durable stores a Space touches (sandbox-manager process output and snapshots, notification and feed projections, agent_memory and Letta), commit the typed ZDR refusal UI, and add a cross-plane ZDR test matrix. Keep telemetry content-free; add a consent gate only if analytics are ever added.
whyItMatters: ZDR is a stated Verevon promise and an architecture rule (it must propagate). Any plane that ignores it is a compliance defect that a regulated buyer will find. GrokBot shows the pattern users expect: a persistent feature is blocked with a visible reason instead of silently storing.

others: qm, teams, buzz (consent-gated or scrubbed telemetry)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: ZDR-blocks-persistence: 1 of 5 (grokbot), unique. Consent-gated, scrubbed telemetry: 4 of 5 (grokbot, qm, teams, buzz), table-stakes.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: The backend reports privacy mode; every persistent feature checks it at connect or write time and returns a typed no-storage error that the UI maps to a visible block state with a reason. For telemetry, analytics start disabled or deferred with a capped buffer until consent resolves, are dropped on opt-out, use closed label sets and scrub errors before send.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: Session Core ignores the claim, so ZDR is enforced at the edge (gateway, Control, notification-core) but not at the store that persists threads and memory. No cross-plane test proves every durable write path refuses under ZDR; the sandbox-manager and agent_memory paths are unchecked; the typed refusal UI is uncommitted. Telemetry hygiene is currently fine because no third-party SDK was found, but nothing guards it.

approachOriginal: Model Plane: in session-core CreateThread, message append and agent_memory writes, branch on claims.zero_data_retention and either persist nothing or return a typed zdr_persistence_unavailable status; model-gateway maps it to the existing typed refusal codes; letta-bridge and sandbox-manager (workspace, snapshot, process output) take the same flag from the decision. Application Plane: Space-originated notifications under ZDR carry reference-only payloads (coordinate with category 05 notification work). Frontend Plane: commit zdr-refusals.ts and render one block state per refusal code. Add a ZDR conformance test (one case per durable write path, per plane) and a CI label allowlist so Prometheus labels and error reports stay content-free. Only if analytics are added: consent state machine with a capped deferred buffer.
dependencies: ZDR claim carried in every plane contract
planeOwner: Model Plane (session-core, model-gateway, sandbox-manager) with Application Plane and Frontend Plane
risks: Feature regressions for ZDR orgs (persistent computers, memory, schedules) must be explicit rather than silent. A missing claim must fail closed. Pre-existing rows written before a posture change are a retention question, handled by the retention item.

alreadyPlanned.where: Planned but not finished: the session-core code comment marks provider/retention propagation as a later slice; apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md S6.1 and S6.2 list ZDR verification cases.

verevon.exactGap: Session Core already enforces ZDR on the caller's verified token claim (authorize_operation refuses every non-read scope on CreateThread, AppendMessage and StartRun, MemoryRetention plus authorize_memory_preflight gate durable and Letta memory, run output is refused and a ZDR managed start is metadata-only); only the Space decision's own zero_data_retention flag is still decoded and discarded (grpc.rs:1749-1755), which Control and the gateway make unreachable today. Execution-core, letta-bridge, notification-core, Quarry and Control also refuse, and a typed refusal catalogue (mp-contracts zdr_refusal.rs, api/contracts/zdr-refusals.json), a posture-matrix golden and the SPA presentation module zdr-refusals.ts (wired into the Space composer through translateApiError) exist, but the catalogue, retention receipts, matrix test and SPA module are still untracked in git. Real remaining gaps: Session Core's own refusals are plain strings rather than typed codes, per-Space ZDR is explicitly 'not applied in v1' (matrix policy.space_zdr, honest-limits L14), sandbox-manager has no ZDR flag (covered only by execution-core's upstream refusal), the README-referenced scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh is missing, and no content-free telemetry label guard was found.
reuse: mp-contracts zdr_refusal catalogue (codes, actions, feature vocabulary) and its golden zdr-refusals.json.
zdr-posture-matrix.json with the strict loader test zdr_retention_matrix.rs as the cross-plane conformance spine.
Session Core MemoryRetention (Durable, ZeroDataRetention, WaivedRun) and retention_receipt.rs as the single posture derivation.
model-gateway grpc_auth.rs, which already maps a ZDR identity to the typed durable-mutation refusal for gateway-side checks.
SPA zdr-refusals.ts plus translateApiError, which the Space composer already uses.
verevon.constraints: ZDR must propagate and a missing claim must fail closed (already the case). Space-level ZDR needs a Control decision, not a UI flag: the posture matrix pins space_zdr as 'changes nothing' until a deliberate change. A Space is a durable shared transcript by design, so Session Core already refuses Space thread creation and appends for ZDR callers; the product decision is how that is worded, not whether to enforce it. Under ZDR, continuation descriptors for approvals are refused (agent.rs:4558-4575), so approvals cannot resume by design. Keep telemetry content-free (gateway metrics are Prometheus-only).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Replace 'Session Core must act on the decision flag' with a small hardening list: (1) commit the untracked catalogue, retention receipt, matrix test and SPA module; (2) return the typed durable-mutation refusal from authorize_operation and memory_grpc preflight instead of plain strings; (3) cross-check the decision's zero_data_retention against caller.zdr() in the Space decision verifiers so a ZDR-flagged decision can never persist; (4) record the Space-ZDR product decision (L14) and add a sandbox-manager flag only if leases ever become reachable by ZDR callers; (5) restore or drop the README's zdr-contract-sync script and add a label allowlist check for Prometheus and error reports.
verevon.effortNote: M to S: the enforcement matrix, typed catalogue and cross-plane refusals are built; what is left is committing work in progress, typing two refusal sites, one cross-check and a product note. Applying per-Space ZDR would be a separate M or L item.
verevon.verdictReason: Largely exists in the code, and the item's central premise (Session Core ignores ZDR and must be made to refuse durable thread, message and memory writes) misdescribes the state. Keep only the residual hardening above and move it out of the W1 priority slot.

reference.corrections: GrokBot's ZDR block is confirmed for one feature: connecting to the persistent sandbox box ('sand box') under privacy mode raises a typed no-storage ConnectError that the UI maps to a block state. The mechanism's 'every persistent feature checks it at connect or write time' generalises from that single case. Say 'GrokBot blocks its persistent computer (sandbox) under privacy mode with a typed no-storage error'. Telemetry 'consent-gated or scrubbed: 4 of 5 (grokbot, qm, teams, buzz)' is wrong for qm. qm backend error reporting is operator opt-in (on only when a DSN is set), and its docs state events and traces are sent unredacted and unscrubbed. qm is a counter-example (record qm-architecture-139 says the same), not a reference. buzz's evidence is server-side operational metrics with closed label sets, not user consent. Correct to: consent-deferred client analytics 1 of 5 (grokbot, 256-event cap, disabled on opt-out); diagnostic data viewer 1 of 5 (teams, REA strings); closed-label operational metrics (buzz); qm opt-in but unredacted. Teams AI-interaction retention is DOC only.
